newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X CEO confident in Busang assays.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X CEO confident in Busang assays.

text.p: The chief executive of Canadian mining firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday he was confident of the accuracy of assay results and the calculation of resources contained in Indonesia's Busang gold find.

In a statement from the company headquarters in Calgary, Alberta, CEO David Walsh said, "The company's board of directors has absolute confidence in the integrity and accuracy of assay results and resource calculations reported by the company for the Busang gold find since inception of exploration in 1993".

The statement said that a Bre-X technical team under the direction of vice-president John Felderhof "has arrived in Jakarta to ensure continuity of the process that will secure the expeditious development of the Busang gold deposit".
Bre-X announced on February 17 that the latest estimates of reserves in the Busang find in East Kalimantan province amounted to 70.95 million ounces of gold.
Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc, with a 15 percent stake in Busang, is currently conducting a due diligence process on the site before developing a mine.
Bre-X has a 45 percent stake in Busang, and Indonesian interests 40 percent.

Shares in Bre-X on the Toronto Stock Exchange fell Canadian $2.80 to a 52-week low of $14.65 on Friday after a report in the Indonesian newspaper Harian Ekonomi Neraca cast doubt on the size of the Busang deposit -- at 71 million ounces the largest find of the century.
The company was also hit by the loss of its chief geologist, Filipino Michael de Guzman, who fell to his death from a helicopter on his way to the Busang property last Wednesday.
Search and rescue officials said on Monday his body had been found on Sunday.
